title: Promise and Orchard
premise: Coral Oyelaran, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and cautious part-time novelist, joins her coastal town's anonymous pen-pal festival meant to pair strangers — but a clerical error pairs her with Jonah Adeyemi, the man whose family's development deal threatens to bulldoze her grandmother's orchard, and whom she publicly humiliated at last year's council meeting. Forced to correspond without knowing each other's identities at first, they fall for the words before discovering the truth, splitting loyalty against honesty just as the orchard's inheritance papers come due. At the festival's final night, Coral must choose between the safe life she rebuilt and testifying for Jonah against his own family firm; she lets him stay past the last train, and together they save the orchard by turning it into a trust co-owned by the town.
about_author: Marguerite Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing love letters in coastal county records before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burn romances set in small towns where weather, paperwork, and pride are the true antagonists.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She tends the lighthouse, drafts her stalled novel, and signs up for the town's anonymous pen-pal festival on a whim — then learns the pairing system has glitched, matching 'enemies' as an experiment. Emotional beat: restless loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Dear Adversary
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He receives his pen-pal assignment and realizes with horror it's Coral — but the rules forbid revealing identity, so he writes anyway under his pseudonym. Their first letters are barbed, brilliant sparring. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her grandmother's health falters, and the inheritance papers reveal the orchard will lapse to the Adeyemi development firm unless Coral files a counter-claim within weeks. She vents to her anonymous pen pal, not knowing who he is. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Letters in Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The correspondence softens into genuine intimacy — shared childhood wounds, his estrangement from his father's firm, her abandoned engagement. Both begin rearranging their days around the mailbox. Emotional beat: falling in love with a stranger.

chapters.title: The Man at the Counter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the festival's midweek social, she nearly recognizes Jonah's voice behind his mask; a near-kiss in the orchard at dusk is interrupted by news that demolition surveys have begun. Emotional beat: desire colliding with dread.

chapters.title: Signed, Your Enemy
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He discovers Coral is his pen pal first — and that his father has used his survey access to fast-track the orchard seizure. Guilt-ridden, he confesses everything in a letter he never sends. Emotional beat: cowardice versus conscience.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She uncovers the truth at the worst moment — reading his unsent confession left in the festival post office. Feeling betrayed twice over, she burns her draft counter-claim and retreats to the lighthouse. Emotional beat: heartbreak weaponized into self-protection.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He publicly breaks with his father at a firm board meeting, leaking documents proving the development deal was built on forged signatures — including his own. He loses his family, his job, and possibly Coral. Emotional beat: costly redemption.

chapters.title: The Festival's Final Night
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the closing ceremony, unmaskings are traditional; Jonah takes the stage and reveals himself before the whole town, offering Coral the floor instead of an apology. She chooses truth over loyalty to her own fear and files the counter-claim aloud. Emotional beat: climax — courage as a public act.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later: the orchard becomes a town trust with Jonah as its first steward, her novel finds its ending, and her grandmother watches them plant a new row of trees. When the last festival train pulls away, Coral asks Jonah to miss the next one too. Emotional beat: home as a choice, made twice.
